$comment: The data flows between Jamie's systems: every hop content takes, who owns each field, and what watches each hop today. This file is the contract; shared/flows.html is rendered from it by `node shared/build-flows.mjs`. A hop is a row here before it is code anywhere. Times are America/Chicago unless a cron says otherwise.

kinds.thing: an entry in Things I've built
kinds.audio: an issue's audio edition or an episode's MP3
kinds.category: a blog post's categories, and a category's description
kinds.note: the note on a saved link
kinds.activity: a Strava activity event: public id, change type and time only

systems.name: Pinboard
systems.fact: posts/update gives the time of the last change; the sync probe reads it with the pinboard_token key of the sync-runtime secret (since 2026-10-26).
systems.notes: Jamie's capture tool for links. No webhooks.

systems.name: micro.blog
systems.fact: The blog's feed shows the newest post; Micropub q=source shows a post's stored source. The rendered page can lag a Micropub write until micro.blog rebuilds.
systems.notes: Source of authority for the blog. Three writers: Jamie, WT Builder's mirror, the Library Agent.

systems.name: Tinylytics
systems.fact: Site and page view counts over its API (key needed).

systems.name: WT Builder
systems.fact: Every send puts a `published` event on the publishing bus (EventBridge bus `thingelstad-publishing`, owned by the sync stack; since 2026-10-27): product, kind, id, which leg went out and when, and every leg sent so far. The sync probe records it as WT Builder's fact and shows the item's journey from that moment. get_status (MCP) shows each issue's send legs; list_events shows what was sent when.
systems.notes: Authors and publishes each issue, and makes Another Thing since 2026-10-11 (that send has not run yet).

systems.name: Library Agent
systems.fact: Its run report under tmp/blog-round/<day>.md, and the blog_round events in the library.
systems.notes: Codex automation, daily 05:00. Runs the library round on the Mac (the one runner with the Tinylytics key), then files categories, fills alt and proposes Featured.

systems.name: Weekly Thing (web)
systems.fact: feed.xml and /archive/ show the newest issue; apps/site/archive/<n>.md on main is the issue's source.
systems.notes: Render surface. Source of authority for issues once sent.

systems.name: Buttondown
systems.fact: The newest email in the account.
systems.notes: The email edition. WT Builder makes a draft; Jamie sends it. A signed subscriber-count webhook is prepared in sync-intake, disabled until its key and explicit enable flag are set; it never changes this email-edition fact.

systems.name: files.thingelstad.com
systems.fact: An object exists at the URL the issue or episode names.

systems.name: Another Thing
systems.notes: Podcast publish surface. Episodes so far were committed by hand.

systems.name: Linking Things
systems.fact: /links.json and /issues.json; links_stats (MCP) gives last_saved and latest_issue; data/sync.json holds Pinboard's stamp and the fetch time.
systems.notes: Every public link since 2005, built from a nightly commit.

systems.name: Things I've built
systems.fact: The registry on the site; activity.xml carries each day's collected observations.
systems.notes: Content changes by pull request; a daily collector refreshes observations. Its public registry supplies the reviewed webhook repository allowlist; private repositories and unlisted pushes are refused. The intake is disabled until its signing key and explicit enable flag are set.

systems.name: Librarian
systems.fact: Each corpus object in S3 carries its fact as metadata (newest-id, newest-at, item-count, built-at; since 2026-10-26): a HEAD says the newest item of each kind the uploaded corpus holds. latest_content and corpus_stats (MCP) show the same from the deployed corpus; library.db in S3 holds what the library pulled.
systems.notes: The library (library.db in S3), the five corpora, and the API Thingy and MCP clients answer from.

systems.name: Thingy
systems.fact: librarian.thingelstad.com/health reports source_revision and corpus_versions, the S3 versions of the corpus objects the running build was deployed against (since 2026-10-26): where they match the objects' current versions, Thingy serves what the Librarian holds; where one differs, the redeploy that serves the newer upload has not landed.
systems.notes: Chat client of the Librarian API. MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex) read the same corpus through librarian.thingelstad.com/mcp.

systems.name: cards.thingelstad.com
systems.fact: A card URL returns an image drawn from the post as it is now.
systems.notes: Draws each post's social card from its h-entry on request; CloudFront caches it.

systems.name: Strava
systems.fact: No activity body is published on the sync page. Signed webhooks may carry only the configured athlete's activity id, change type and event time to the private publishing bus.
systems.notes: Intake starts disabled. The current official webhook example defines X-Strava-Signature (timestamp and HMAC-SHA256); no activity fetch or post is made.

systems.name: Publishing bus
systems.fact: thingelstad-publishing carries scoped event metadata in its ninety-day archive. Webhook bodies and athlete/subscriber identities never reach the public sync files.
systems.notes: Owned by sync.thingelstad.xyz. Buttondown, GitHub and Strava intake senders each wait for their signing key and explicit enable flag; this node publishes no activity fact.

The captured public feed has tags but no independent numeric Micropub uid or modification time: authenticated q=source stays behind that explicit reader TODO. hops.moves: An episode: the mastered MP3 into the audio bucket, then its page and transcript in one commit.
hops.mechanism: The Another Thing send (/another), built 2026-10-11. Since 2026-10-26 (wt-builder PR #8) it puts the tagged MP3 in the another-site audio bucket at uploads/YYYY/another-thing-N.mp3 with the AWS key in WT Builder's .env, reads it back, then commits the episode page (with audioBytes and audioSeconds) and its transcript to git. No MP3 goes to git; CloudFront serves the bucket at the same /uploads/ URL.
hops.verify: podcast.xml carries the episode. Its receipt is the published event for the another leg on the bus; the sync page measures the hop from that event's time.
hops.notes: Never run. Episodes so far were committed by hand, their MP3s put with npm run audio:put. Needs ANOTHER_GITHUB_PAT_TOKEN. The send behaves as audio:put: the same bytes are left alone, different audio at the key is refused unless an earlier send of the episode put it there, nothing deletes from the bucket. The deploy-aws job refuses a feed whose MP3 is not in the bucket at the feed's length. Arrival reporting contract (sync plan step 4): source another, detail-type received, detail { system, kind, id, at, url, via } on thingelstad-publishing. It observes this hop; it does not trigger or repair it. The destination sender and its scoped permission wait for step 5; none is enabled by this note. Step 6 leaves hand-published episodes with the public podcast feed as their producer. This row remains unverified until the first WT Builder another send announces itself; no episode is invented to change the status. Step 5 sender contract: Another Thing reports source another, received, kind episode, via site-deploy after the public feed matches its build and changes from a known prior episode. An unchanged deploy or unknown baseline sends no arrival. This reporting does not turn the manual producer into a WT Builder send; its proposed sender and delivery-role permission wait for PR review and Jamie's activation.

hops.moves: The configured athlete's activity id, create/update/delete type and event time, never a title, route, owner id or body.
hops.mechanism: sync-intake /strava verifies the timestamped X-Strava-Signature over raw bytes, accepts activity objects for the configured owner only, and puts source strava, detail-type activity. No subscriber or content write follows.
hops.verify: A natural signed delivery is acknowledged by EventBridge as metadata { id, type, at }. Fixtures and mocks prove parsing without real activity. The public page contains no webhook body.
hops.notes: Off until Jamie adds strava_webhook_signing_key and the separate strava_webhook_verify_token to sync-runtime, confirms the signing contract for his app, supplies its owner id and enables EnableStrava. The official API requires a 200 for successful POSTs and the GET challenge; invalid requests still return empty 204. No real activity is manufactured to test it. What consumes these events is Jamie's later decision.

watchers.name: sync.thingelstad.xyz
watchers.where: AWS Lambda on a half-hour schedule and on every published event (then again at 2, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes), publishing a public page
watchers.sees: Whether the destination of each hop holds the newest item of its kind, measured from the published event or the next fact down; each item's journey, system by system, with the time it was first seen at each. The received contract accepts destination-reported arrival times, labelled reported; unmatched item ids wait at most one hour. Destination senders wait for their own step-5 PRs. New public blog posts are announced by the sync function as microblog published events; a first baseline is observation, not a historical send. Stored-source/Library Agent receipt fields remain an explicit TODO, with no destination-only inference for hop 19.
watchers.misses: A hop whose ends publish no fact (Buttondown, Tinylytics); whether the content is right.

watchers.name: weekly-thing-feed-publication-monitor
watchers.where: OpenClaw cron on the Mac, 12:00 daily, posts to Discord
watchers.sees: A new item in weekly's feed.xml or podcast.xml.

watchers.name: another-thing-podcast-feed-monitor
watchers.where: OpenClaw cron on the Mac, 08:15 daily, posts to Discord

watchers.sees: Failed, disabled or stale OpenClaw jobs.
watchers.misses: Jobs outside OpenClaw: launchd, GitHub Actions, Codex automations.

watchers.name: Thingy drift check
watchers.where: GitHub Actions in thingy.thingelstad.com, 06:17 daily, files or closes a GitHub issue
watchers.sees: The vendored Librarian contract and MCP surface drifting from librarian-thing main; npm advisories.

watchers.name: CloudWatch alarms (Thingy, Librarian API, Linking Things MCP)

watchers.sees: 5xx rates, auth bursts, throttling, dead letters, the subscribe path.
watchers.misses: Whether the data is current. No alarm anywhere measures lag.

watchers.sees: A red run, including a blog pull skipped for a missing key.
watchers.misses: Nobody is notified of a red scheduled run.

watchers.name: nightly.log
watchers.misses: A green run that joined a stale checkout (hop 6, 2026-10-26).

watchers.where: projects-sysadmin: config/activity.toml routes, scripts/activity, stack projects-activity-alarms; posts land in the otto-discord Activity category (#publishing-log, #sites-log, #sysadmin-log; #needs-jamie for BLOCKED, NEEDS JAMIE, FAILED and firing alarms); every post in ~/Library/Logs/projects-activity/events.jsonl. Built 2026-10-26.
watchers.sees: Agent closeouts per channel; every CloudWatch alarm state change in the account, routed by alarm-name prefix (weekly-thing-librarian-, thingy-web-, weekly-site-, another-site- to #publishing-log; links-, thingelstad-xyz-, cards- to #sites-log); Codex automations that fired but started no run (activity missed, in the 06:30 brief); each published send leg on the publishing bus, as one post in #publishing-log saying which legs have gone and which are pending (rule projects-activity-published in the projects-activity-alarms stack, since 2026-10-26).
watchers.misses: Lag itself, until the sync alarms exist (step 4, prefix sync-); a leg that never sends (no event, so no post; the sync page shows it moving, then late).
